items.grounds: Adversarial re-derivation, both directions. The shipped rationale's sole anti-division warrant is the undigited universal 'no new narrative-onset marker -- a fresh time-frame or scene turn -- recurs to divide it' (no sweep digit anywhere in the field). Against the bytes: (1) the row's own splice opens MT 20:2 verse-initially with the time-frame "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא" (oshb:Isa.20.2, byte tier), which stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide, both verse-initial (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier - oshb:Isa.18.7, oshb:Isa.20.2); (2) the scene-turn formula "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒" (oshb:Isa.20.6, byte tier) stands verse-internally in the span's own closing verse, one of 45 verses book-wide carrying it (sweep: 45 verses, skeleton tier), 13 of those in chs 19-24 - 6 inside Isa.19.16-Isa.19.25 and 7 beyond, Isa.20.6 among them, exactly the digit set the preceding shipped row structures its series on; (3) the interior seam the row argues down, Isa.20.2|Isa.20.3 before the verse-initial divine-speech onset "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), is where the inventory records a setumah at Isa.20.2 (SAMEKH, single-witness). Every factual leg of the finding re-derives exactly. Tested for the row: the whole-chapter sign-act reading stays content-defensible, the 20:2 frame is readable as part of the opening complex, and confidence already sits at the whole-chapter medium_low cap - so the defect is a defective, undigited exclusivity warrant contradicted by the span's own bytes, not alone load-bearing. Confirm at medium.

Re-derived from MT 21:11: the watchman nouns are tokens 6 and 9 of the verse, "שֹׁמֵר֙" and "שֹׁמֵ֖ר" (oshb:Isa.21.11, byte tier each); consonants and vowel points are identical and only the cantillation differs (U+0599 in the first, U+0596 in the second), so the pair's strongest mutual tier is accent_stripped - the collate truth the tier-disclosure standard requires the prose to name; byte / accent_stripped / skeleton are never conflated. The shipped clause 'the watchman noun repeats at skeleton tier' therefore names a tier below the truth. The paired clause survives testing both ways: the night-forms "מִלַּ֔יְלָה" and "מִלֵּֽיל" (oshb:Isa.21.11, byte tier each) match at no tier against each other - their consonantal skeletons already differ. The misstatement sits inside boundary_rationale as a warrant-support claim but is not load-bearing: the verse-initial massa header at oshb:Isa.21.11 carries the seam and is untouched, as the finding itself rules. Confirm at medium; the proposed one-clause tier repair is the right cure.

Re-derived: the row's span is Isa.21.13-Isa.21.15, so its closing seam is Isa.21.15|Isa.21.16. The bow noun stands as "קֶ֣שֶׁת" (oshb:Isa.21.15, byte tier) in the row's own closing verse and as "קֶ֛שֶׁת" (oshb:Isa.21.17, byte tier) two verses past the seam; the two forms' strongest mutual tier is accent_stripped (cantillation alone differs), and the row's digit re-derives (sweep: 3 verses in chs 20-23 - oshb:Isa.21.15, oshb:Isa.21.17, oshb:Isa.22.3). One site in-span plus one beyond the seam: the recurrence does straddle the row's own closing seam, so the shipped sentence 'it does not straddle this row's own seam' is false as geometry, and its 'since' clause - that the divine-speech onset "כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י" (oshb:Isa.21.16, byte tier) remains the seam warrant - argues survival, not non-straddling: the conflation the finding names. Tested for the row: sites, tier and digit are all honestly disclosed and the seam warrant genuinely survives, so this is a misstated cross-seam disclosure, not a load-bearing defect. Confirm at medium.

Re-derived: MT 22:12 opens "וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.12, byte tier) - the day formula is tokens 5-6 of the verse, not verse-initial. The formula recurs across both of this row's seams: mid-verse at tokens 6-7 of MT 22:8, "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.8, byte tier), inside the preceding shipped span, accent_stripped against the 22:12 form; byte-identical at tokens 2-3 of MT 22:20, "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier), beyond the closing seam; and verse-initial at MT 22:25, "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.25, byte tier), accent_stripped against 22:12. The shipped row leads observed_substrate_signals with oracle_frame.scene_shift and opens its rationale on that formula, yet discloses none of the recurrences and carries none of oshb:Isa.22.8 / oshb:Isa.22.20 / oshb:Isa.22.25 in boundary_evidence_refs - undisclosed cross-seam cohesion on the row's own declared driver. The immediately preceding shipped row rules this very seam the other way (the formula is cohesion, not a driver; the warrant is the fresh grammatical subject entering at oshb:Isa.22.12), and no fresh-subject key appears in this row's signals. Tested for the row: its own prose does call the opening 'a fresh divine summons', and the cut itself survives on the fresh-subject warrant, so the boundary stands and the defect is the mis-declared driver plus the missing disclosure. Confirm at medium.

Re-derived from the eight tokens of MT 22:20, "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ" (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier): no token carries a second-person suffix or form - no kaf-sofit anywhere in the verse - and there is no imperative and no vocative; the newly named steward enters with prefixed lamed as the object of the first-person verb in "וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים" (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier), rendered first-person in the second witness too, “I will call my servant Eliakim” (web:Isa.22.20). The 2ms addressee chain that closes this row's span - the entire verse "וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ" (oshb:Isa.22.19, byte tier), every token 2ms-suffixed - resumes one verse past the seam in "כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙" (oshb:Isa.22.21, byte tier): the grammatical addressee is unchanged across the seam. The shipped closing warrant ('opens the next unit on its own addressee shift'; 'the cut still stands on the verse-initial addressee-specific commission opening the following verse') is byte-false: MT 22:20 is neither an addressee shift nor a commission to an addressee - contrast the row's own opening imperatives "לֶךְ בֹּא֙" (oshb:Isa.22.15, byte tier), which do commission. The row contradicts itself (its device_notes disclose the 2ms chain crossing this same seam), ships at high confidence, and carries oracle_frame.addressee_shift; the neighboring shipped row reads the same bytes correctly (referent as object of the divine verb, addressee carried over). A byte-false load-bearing closing-seam warrant: confirm at high. The seam itself survives on the finding's replacement warrants (verse-initial day-formula onset, fresh named referent as object), so no span change follows.

Re-derived: this row's declared lead driver opens MT 22:20 as "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier, tokens 1-3, the verse-opening construction); the two-word formula inside it is byte-identical to "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.12, byte tier) - a site across this row's opening seam Isa.22.19|Isa.22.20, inside the shipped span Isa.22.12-Isa.22.14 - and stands mid-verse at tokens 6-7 of MT 22:8, "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.8, byte tier), accent_stripped against the 22:20 form. The shipped row discloses only the 2ms address chain as cross-seam continuity: the byte-true recurrence of its own lead driver is undisclosed, the distinguisher the cut actually rests on - verse-opening position at 22:20 against mid-verse position at 22:8 (tokens 6-7) and 22:12 (tokens 5-6) - is never stated, and boundary_evidence_refs carries neither oshb:Isa.22.12 nor oshb:Isa.22.8. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule an undisclosed byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row - here that device is the declared driver itself. Tested for the row: the closing side is properly handled (the renewed verse-initial formula and postpositive signature at oshb:Isa.22.25 are named), and the cut independently rests on the declared named-referent-as-object signal at the seam verse, so the defect is disclosure, not the boundary. Confirm at medium.

Re-derived: the shipped rationale's only closing-edge statement is that the consecration run "קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.23.18, byte tier) 'closes both this row and the chapter' - a chapter-division fact, tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence - and boundary_evidence_refs carries nothing across the Isa.23.18|Isa.24.1 seam (no web:Isa.24.1, no oshb:Isa.24.1), all at high confidence. A tier-1 onset is available and unused: MT 24:1 opens verse-initially with "הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה" (oshb:Isa.24.1, byte tier), the third-person judgment announcement the following shipped row argues from. The row's petuchah disclosure at oshb:Isa.23.18 (PE, single-witness) re-derives against the inventory, and its device_notes disclaimer correctly keeps the mark in the corroboration lane - but a device_notes disclaimer does not repair the rationale's own closing warrant. The opening edge re-derives sound: MT 23:15 opens verse-initially with "וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (oshb:Isa.23.15, byte tier). The boundary is real and independently derivable, so the defect is a mis-laned closing warrant with one-sided refs, not a wrong seam: confirm at medium; the proposed repair (name the oshb:Isa.24.1 onset, add the far-side refs, re-cut the chapter clause, re-check confidence) is the right cure.
